title: FCM clearing concentration and high-volatility crowding-out of small commodity traders
verdict_scope: NULL means the negative, binary high-vol crowding-out hypothesis (spec1 fcm_x_highvol < 0) is NOT SUPPORTED. 'Not supported' is the whole claim: these estimators cannot establish that the effect is absent, and NULL does NOT mean 'no association'. The continuous analogue (spec2 fcm_x_rvz) is POSITIVE and significant: coef 2.8747e-04, t_DK 2.54, t_cluster_month 2.56 -- i.e. in the direction opposite to crowding-out.
claim_language_rule: NO specification here supports a predictive, causal, forecast or known-before-outcome claim, and none supports 'there is no predictability'. spec1-3 are ex-post association because the FCM report can become available mid-outcome-month while the outcome is a whole-month average change. spec4 hardens the timing (month-start as-of merge, point-in-time regime label at t-1, t-2 DCOT controls, its own sample) but its ex-ante status is CONDITIONAL on the synthetic availability constant, so its null reads 'an association is NOT SUPPORTED under this timing arrangement' -- not 'no association', and not 'no predictability'. Every null here is stated as NOT SUPPORTED, never as an absence and never as disproved.

data_provenance.fcm_source: CFTC Financial Data for FCMs (monthly xlsx)
data_provenance.fcm_publication_lag_is_synthetic: avail_date = month_end + 45d is a constant chosen by this script, not an observed CFTC release date; the offline cache carries no release date column. Sensitivity over 30/45/60/75/90d lives in K1694_lag_sensitivity.json.
data_provenance.fcm_asof_merge_primary: backward as-of: latest FCM report whose synthetic avail_date <= the outcome month_end. Availability may therefore fall INSIDE the outcome month -- association timing, not predictive timing.
data_provenance.fcm_asof_merge_spec4: backward as-of on the outcome month's START, so the report's ASSUMED availability precedes the whole outcome window. Assumed, not verified -- see fcm_publication_lag_is_synthetic.
data_provenance.dcot_source: CFTC DCOT futures-only 72hh-3qpy (weekly; as-of Tue, published Fri)
data_provenance.vol_source: yfinance daily futures; monthly realized vol = std(daily logret)*sqrt(252)

sample.estimation_sample_owner: build_spec_frame() for spec1-3 and both bootstraps; build_lagged_frame() for spec4, selected by spec4's own regressors
sample.panel_span_completeness_basis: every retained row's DCOT month is CERTIFIED continuous -- at least 4 reports, no gap over 9 days between consecutive reports including the entry gap from the previous month, so a skipped week anywhere fails. Its RV month is only SCREENED: the day count must match the CME futures calendar to within one day, which cannot rule out a one-day truncation common to every commodity. No partial month such as 2026-07 survives either test, but 'complete months only' would overstate the RV side. See sample.completeness.rule.rv_residual_blind_spot.

effective_temporal_dof.reading: the FCM factor is one system-wide monthly series and is highly persistent, so the effective temporal degrees of freedom are well BELOW the calendar-month count; the months must not be called independent

rule.dcot_month_complete: nweeks >= 4 AND every gap between consecutive reports <= 9d, INCLUDING the entry gap from the previous month's last report AND month_end - last_report <= 6d
rule.dcot_rule_detects: a skipped week anywhere, first week included, because continuity is measured against the previous report rather than against the month boundary: deleting any single report makes one gap about 14 days (observed gaps in this cache are only 6, 7 or 8 days). A month with no earlier report at all -- the first month of the series -- can never be certified and is dropped.
rule.rv_month_complete: trading days >= 15 AND expected_trading_days - trading days <= 2 AND max(trading days across commodities that month) - trading days <= 2 AND expected_trading_days - max(trading days that month) <= 1
rule.rv_expected_trading_days_definition: weekdays minus the CME futures holiday calendar -- New Year (not rolled back to 31 Dec when 1 Jan is a Saturday), MLK, Presidents' Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth from 2022, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas -- minus the enumerated unscheduled closures in rv_unscheduled_closures. Columbus Day and Veterans Day are federal holidays on which CME futures TRADE and are deliberately not subtracted: subtracting them understated the count and refuted this rule's own detection claim (Codex round 4, 2020-10).

rv_unscheduled_closures.2012-10-29: Hurricane Sandy: U.S. markets closed (day 1 of 2)
rv_unscheduled_closures.2012-10-30: Hurricane Sandy: U.S. markets closed (day 2 of 2)
rv_unscheduled_closures.2018-12-05: national day of mourning for George H. W. Bush

rule.rv_rule_detects: an independently truncated download (a commodity short of both the calendar and its peers) AND a truncation common to every commodity of 2 or more days, which no cross-sectional check can see -- except in the 6 months listed under rv_months_observed_beyond_the_cme_calendar, where some contract prints an abbreviated holiday session, so the threshold there is the per-month figure given in that list
rule.rv_endpoint_test: UNAVAILABLE for this cache: rv_monthly.csv stores day counts only, no first/last observation dates. build_vol() now records them, so any regenerated cache upgrades this to a true endpoint test.
rule.rv_residual_blind_spot: a truncation of exactly ONE day common to every commodity is indistinguishable, in a count-only cache, from an unscheduled market closure -- and by the same token an entry in rv_unscheduled_closures rests on the external event that dated it, not on anything this cache can show. Two such closures are in sample and are subtracted by name: 2012-10 (Hurricane Sandy) and 2018-12 (national day of mourning). This rule therefore does NOT prove each download reached both ends of its month; it SCREENS the day count for consistency with the CME futures calendar to within one day, wider by the excess shown in rv_months_observed_beyond_the_cme_calendar. Months that pass are screened, NOT certified complete: certifying them from a count-only cache would need independent endpoint evidence, which this frozen rv_monthly.csv does not carry.
rule.effect_of_dcot_incomplete: row dropped from the panel entirely
rule.effect_of_rv_incomplete: rv masked to NaN; DCOT row retained
rule.adjacency: first differences and their lags are voided whenever the previous retained month is not the immediately preceding calendar month, so dropping a month cannot silently create a two-month difference

spec1_fcm_highvol.note: ex-post association: the FCM report may become available mid-outcome-month and the outcome is a whole-month average change

spec2_fcm_rvz_continuous.note: ex-post association; same timing caveat as spec1

spec3_trader_conc4_highvol.note: ex-post association; sample is smaller wherever conc4 is missing

spec4_lagged_timing_hardened.note: lagged design, ex-ante ONLY CONDITIONAL on the synthetic FCM availability constant; not a verified predictive test

bootstrap_spec1.headline: stationary_block_by_month

month_cluster_iid.label: IID month-cluster bootstrap (NOT a block bootstrap; preserves the within-month cross-section but destroys month-to-month serial correlation)

bootstrap_spec1.design_matrix_note: Both bootstraps resample months of the SAME build_spec_frame() rows and refit the SAME SPEC1_RHS (time trend `t` included), so the CI is the CI of the reported spec1 coefficient.

spec2_continuous_interaction_is_positive.reading: opposite sign to the crowding-out hypothesis; it is why the NULL must not be stated as 'no association'

spec4_lagged_timing_hardened.reading: an association is NOT SUPPORTED under this timing arrangement. That is not the same as showing there is none, and it is not evidence of 'no predictability': the FCM leg's ex-ante status is conditional on the synthetic availability constant, never verified.

limitations: FCM concentration is a single system-wide monthly series; its main effect is a common time factor. The panel has 3276 rows spanning 149 calendar months, and those months are NOT independent: the FCM z-score has ACF(1) 0.964, ACF(6) 0.817, ACF(12) 0.584. Effective temporal degrees of freedom are well below the calendar-month count and no test here quantifies how far below.

FCM publication dates are SYNTHETIC (month_end + 45d), never checked against actual CFTC release dates; the lag grid in K1694_lag_sensitivity.json shows insensitivity to the assumed vintage but is not a verification of it.

Within-month timing overlap: in spec1-3 the FCM report's assumed availability can fall inside the outcome month, and the outcome d_nonrep is the change in a whole-month average, so part of the outcome window predates the signal. Ex-post association only.

Regime labels rv_z and highvol in spec1-3 use FULL-SAMPLE within-commodity moments, i.e. the labelling itself looks ahead. Acceptable for a retrospective association; spec4 uses point-in-time expanding moments instead.

spec4 is a timing-hardened lagged design, NOT a verified ex-ante test. Its FCM leg is dated by the synthetic availability constant, so if the true CFTC release lag exceeds 45 days the report it treats as available at month start was not. Its null therefore reads 'an association is not supported under this timing arrangement', never 'there is no association' and never 'there is no predictability'.

The month-cluster IID bootstrap preserves the within-month cross-section but does NOT preserve month-to-month serial correlation; it is reported only alongside the stationary block bootstrap, which does.

The last weekly DCOT report of month t-1 is published within ~3 days of its Tuesday as-of date, which can land inside month t. spec1-3 keep t-1 controls (they are ex-post specs anyway); spec4 uses t-2 DCOT aggregates so its controls are fully published before the outcome month begins.
Volatility regime is contemporaneous with the outcome in spec1-3 -> association, not causal; reverse causality (small-trader exit affecting vol) cannot be excluded.
FCM seg funds are dominated by financial futures; crowding-out mapped onto physical-commodity small traders is an indirect linkage.
yfinance continuous-futures realized vol is a proxy for each commodity's true vol.
